title: The biggest advertiser in the business
lede: Atari outspent every rival on television. The spending rose fastest in the year the market turned.

blocks.title: Television advertising, first nine months of 1982
blocks.subtitle: $ millions, by video game company.

blocks.title: From $75 million to “low millions”
blocks.body: “In its heyday, Atari alone used to spend $75 million on advertising,” the Times wrote in 1986. That autumn Nintendo planned to spend $16 million, [Sega](/dreamcast/) more than $9 million and Jack Tramiel’s Atari Corporation an amount “in the ‘low millions.’”[^9] The earlier estimate of more than $100 million for 1982 comes from the same newspaper in December 1982.[^1] The two figures were reported four years apart and may not measure the same thing.
